classFaq.rolesQ: Which roles can the {class} play in {game}?
classFaq.rolesA: The {class} has {count} {specsLabel}: {specs}. That lets it play {roles}.
classFaq.rolesRetail: You can switch specializations for free at any time outside of combat, so one character covers all of these roles.
classFaq.rolesForever: Which tree you build is decided by how you spend your talent points. Many players level with a different tree than the one they use in dungeons and raids.
classFaq.armorA: The {class} wears {armor}, {armorNote}. It shares that armor type with the {others}, so you split armor loot with them in groups.

armorNote.plate: the heaviest armor type in the game
armorNote.cloth: the lightest armor type. It takes hits less well and relies on distance, shields and crowd control instead

classFaq.armorForever: As in Classic, it will most likely learn {armor} at level 40 and wear {lighter} before that.

beginnerA.easy: Yes. The {class} is considered beginner friendly: it is sturdy, forgives mistakes and its playstyle clicks quickly. It is a safe pick for your first character.
beginnerA.medium: Somewhat. The basics of the {class} click quickly, but dungeons and raids need a bit more practice than the simplest classes. If you stick with it, you won't stay a beginner for long.
beginnerA.hard: It is better for experienced players. The {class} has lots of tools and rewards experience, so the learning curve is steeper. It still works as a first class if its fantasy excites you: while leveling you learn its abilities one at a time.

classFaq.soloQ: Is the {class} good for solo players?

soloA.good: Yes. The {class} does very well on its own, thanks to self-healing, sturdiness or a companion. Questing, world content and leveling go quickly with little downtime.
soloA.medium: Yes, with some practice. The {class} handles solo play well but needs care when several enemies attack at once. With the right emergency buttons that is easy to manage.
soloA.weak: Not really. The {class} is slower or more vulnerable alone and shines mostly in groups. In dungeons and raids it is all the more welcome.

quest.npcAlt: Thalgrim Oakhorn: a dwarf with a headband and a long, braided red beard
quest.questText:
Ah, a new face! I can see it in your eyes, traveler: too many alts, no main. Believe me, I have trained hundreds like you. Warriors who secretly wanted to heal. Mages who longed for plate armor. Druids who still can't pick a form.

Answer me seven questions. Honestly, and without thinking about tier lists. Then I will tell you which path is truly meant for you.
quest.objective: Answer Thalgrim Oakhorn 7 questions about your playstyle.
quest.rewardGold: Gold: 0 (Thalgrim is a bit short on coin)
declineLines: Decline? Hm. I will pretend I didn't hear that. The question remains, though: which class do you play?
You remind me of a murloc in front of a mirror. Lots of noise, no decision. Mrglglgl.
Fine. Those who won't ask Thalgrim must ask fate. Go roll the dice, traveler.
quest.declineRandom: Let fate roll the dice instead

npcLines.role: Thalgrim crosses his arms: "Let's start with the most important part."
npcLines.range: "Up close or from a distance? Don't worry, I won't call you a coward."
npcLines.content: "And where do you spend your evenings in Azeroth?"
npcLines.complexity: "How many buttons can you handle before your fingers tie themselves in knots?"
npcLines.theme: Thalgrim's eyes sparkle: "Now the heart of it. What makes your heart beat faster?"
npcLines.armor: "Last question. And yes, looks matter. Transmog is the true endgame, after all."

quest.completeText: Thalgrim nods, satisfied: "I knew it from the very first moment. There is a true {class} in you. But take a look at the other two as well, Azeroth rewards curiosity."
